2.content: Assign an extremely large negative penalty (e.g., -1e9) to any move that lands on a hazard cell (H) or places the agent orthogonally adjacent to a hazard. This penalty dominates all other scores, ensuring unsafe moves are never selected.

3.content: Give a large positive score proportional to the reduction in Manhattan distance to the goal caused by a move, and a large negative score proportional to any increase in that distance; moves that leave the distance unchanged receive a modest baseline score.
